content.value_statement: Modern interfaces often feel unclear when motion and feedback are inconsistent. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design accessible transitions, microinteractions, and loading states.
actual_capabilities: Designs button, form, navigation, toast, and gesture feedback patterns.
Provides timing, easing, and spring guidance for UI motion.
Shows loading states, skeleton screens, progress indicators, and success states.
Applies reduced motion and accessibility guidance to animation decisions.
References Framer Motion, CSS transitions, Web Animations API, and scroll animation patterns.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a full design system generator.
It does not test animation performance on real devices by itself.
It assumes the project already has a frontend framework or styling approach.
It does not replace product research or usability testing.

use_cases.title: Polish Checkout Feedback
use_cases.description: Add loading, success, error, and disabled states that make form submission status clear.

use_cases.title: Implement Motion Tokens
use_cases.description: Create consistent timing, easing, and transition guidance for reusable interface components.

use_cases.title: Improve Navigation Transitions
use_cases.description: Plan page, tab, menu, and scroll animations that preserve context during movement.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a single component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this button interaction with clear hover, press, loading, success, and error states. Respect reduced motion preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Design Form Motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for a form workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this form flow and propose interaction patterns for validation, character limits, submission progress, and error recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Create Transition Guidelines
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for a product area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define motion rules for modals, menus, tabs, page transitions, and notifications. Include timing, easing, accessibility, and performance guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Motion System
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert task for an existing application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the current interaction design for inconsistent motion, unclear feedback, performance risks, and accessibility gaps. Prioritize fixes by user impact.

output_examples.input: A save button changes text after users click it, but users miss failures.
output: Recommended states: idle, loading, success, and error.
Use a disabled loading state during submission.
Show a short success confirmation, then return to idle.
Keep the error visible until users retry or edit the form.

output_examples.input: A page transition feels slow and disorienting.
output: Reduce the transition to 200 to 300 milliseconds.
Keep the destination layout stable before the animation starts.
Skip decorative motion when reduced motion is enabled.

output_examples.input: A dashboard needs better loading states for cards and tables.
output: Use skeleton screens that match final layout dimensions.
Keep filters and navigation interactive while data loads.
Use progress indicators only when progress can be measured.
Avoid layout shifts when content replaces placeholders.

best_practices: Use motion to explain state changes, not to decorate every action.
Prefer transform and opacity for smooth animations and lower layout cost.
Respect reduced motion preferences for every meaningful animation.
anti_patterns: Animating width, height, top, or left for frequent UI movement.
Using long transitions that delay user actions or hide feedback.
Adding motion without clear accessibility, performance, or product purpose.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build microinteractions, motion rules, loading states, transitions, and feedback patterns for user interfaces.

faq.question: Can it implement Framer Motion patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference material includes Framer Motion examples for gestures, transitions, layout animation, and scroll effects.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility needs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes reduced motion guidance and recommends motion that supports orientation and feedback.

faq.question: Is it only for React projects?
faq.answer: No. Many examples use React, but the principles also apply to CSS transitions and browser animation APIs.

faq.question: Will it choose visual styling for me?
faq.answer: It can recommend interaction behavior, timing, and feedback. Final brand styling still depends on the product design system.

faq.question: Can it test animation performance automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives performance guidance, but real performance testing must happen in the target application and devices.
